table.title: The Nine Years' Programme of Constitutional Preparation
table.caption_extra: The main outlines of the nine years' programme of preparation for Constitutional Government were as follows :—

rows: Issue of regulations for financial reform.
Establishment of a Bureau for the reform of the Manchu system, particularly as regards the treatment of Bannermen, and the fusion of Manchu and Chinese.
Preparation of elementary lesson-books for teaching reading.
Preparation of books for general reading.
Drafting of Civil, Commercial and Criminal Laws.
Issue of Regulations for the National Assembly.
Taking of census of the whole Empire.
Drafting of Civil Service Examination regulations, and of regulations for official salaries.
Issue of regulations for Judicial Courts.
Local administrative system to be extended to townships.
Report by Viceroys and Governors on census in the provinces.
Endeavour to carry out Provincial Budgets.
Issue of regulations for Civil Service Examinations.
Establishment in all Capitals and Treaty Ports of Judicial Courts (Shenpanting).
Organization of system for auditing Government Accounts.
Investigation of the Budget for the Empire.
Enforcement of Civil Service and Official Salaries regulations.
Establishment of Judicial Courts in Fu's.
Organization of Elementary Schools in all townships.
Consideration of the revised Commercial, Civil and Criminal Laws.
Extension of Local Government system to townships.
Local Government system to be carried out this year.
Issue of new Metropolitan and Provincial Official systems.
Judicial Courts in all cities, towns and townships must be in working order this year.
Endeavour to carry out Budget for the whole Empire.
Organization of Judicial Courts to deal with political matters.
Complete organization of all Judicial Courts in the provinces.
Issue of Civil and Commercial Laws.
Police forces shall be established this year in all towns and villages.
Strict adherence to the Imperial Budget.
One per cent. of the population should be able to read and write in this year.
Abolition of all distinction between Manchu and Chinese.
Enforcement of new Civil and Commercial Laws.
Organization of Police throughout the Empire to be completed.
Two per cent. of the population should be able to read and write in this period.
Issue of regulations for the election of an Upper and a Lower House.
Elections for the Upper and Lower Houses.
Preparation of Budget for the following year for discussion in Parliament.
Organization of a Privy Council, and of Advisory Ministers.
Five per cent. of the population should be able to read and write in this period.

footnotes: [For subsequent modifications introduced at the instance of the National Assembly, v. p. 376.]
